ai.description: *Chamaeleo zeylanicus* (Chamaeleonidae) reaches 37 cm. It is typically green or brown with variable mottling, a casque on the head, and zygodactylous feet. It features independently moving eyes.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Chamaeleo zeylanicus* is best distinguished by its prominent, high-crested casque and the distinct, serrated white scales along its belly midline (ventral crest).
ai.habitat: The Indian chameleon inhabits dry deciduous forests, scrublands, and agricultural hedgerows across the Indian subcontinent, typically at elevations below 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Asian chameleon is primarily diurnal, utilizing its specialized zygodactylous feet and prehensile tail to navigate arboreal habitats while hunting insects with its tongue.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chamaeleo zeylanicus* is oviparous, typically laying a single clutch of 10–30 eggs in a burrow. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, usually between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Chamaeleo zeylanicus* inhabits dry forests and scrublands across peninsular India, Sri Lanka, and parts of Pakistan, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in elevation.
